newsitem.title: CHINA: Few China students return from study abroad.
newsitem.headline: Few China students return from study abroad.

text.p: More than 270,000 students have left China to study abroad in the past 18 years, but only 90,000 have returned, the official People's Daily said on Wednesday.
Since China opened its doors to the West in 1979, only 4,000 of 130,000 students who financed their own overseas education have returned home, the newspaper said.
Of some 44,000 students who won government sponsorship to go abroad, as many as 37,000 have come back, while 48,000 of the 86,000 who were sponsored by their work unit have returned, it said.
The number returning in recent years has improved as China's economy has boomed, it said.

In response to a report that from 1979 to 1995 only 75,000 of 220,000 students abroad had returned, China began a drive to slow the brain drain by fining government-funded students who failed to return on time or changed their plans while overseas.

While graduates with state-funded degrees are generally not permitted to leave China for further study until they have worked for a state enterprise for several years, more and more students are willing to pay their way out.
